+- `Strategy#redirect` now escapes the target URI before interpolating it into the inline `<script>` emitted when the `:iframe` option is enabled. Previously the URI was written verbatim, so a value containing a quote, `</script>`, or a line terminator could break out of the JavaScript string literal and execute in the application's origin (CWE-116/79). The `:iframe` branch also only emits the script for an `http(s)` or relative/protocol-relative target; a `javascript:`, `data:`, or `vbscript:` URI (which escaping cannot neutralize) falls through to the ordinary 302, whose `Location` header is inert. The non-iframe branch now HTML-escapes the URI it writes into the 302 body, and both branches send a `text/html` Content-Type.

+- `Strategy#store_origin` now refuses to persist an `omniauth.origin` (from the origin param or the referer) whose scheme can run as script (`javascript:`, `data:`, `vbscript:`), so any code that later redirects to the stored origin can't execute it. **Behavior change:** an origin param with one of those schemes is dropped and no longer falls back to the referer. Other schemes, including non-web deep links such as `myapp://` used by mobile sign-in, are still stored.
